# 1 Kings Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Solomon sealed a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt by marrying his daughter. He brought her to the City of David while he finished building his palace, the LORD's temple, and the wall around Jerusalem.

**2** The people were still sacrificing at the hilltop shrines, however, because no temple had yet been built for the name of the LORD.

**3** Solomon loved the LORD and followed the practices of his father David — except that he too offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places.

**4** The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, since it was the most important high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on its altar.

**5** That night at Gibeon, the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream. God said, "What do you want? Ask, and I will give it to you."

**6** Solomon replied, "You showed tremendous faithful love to your servant, my father David, because he lived before you with integrity, righteousness, and an honest heart. And you have continued this great faithful love by giving him a son to sit on his throne today.

**7** Now, LORD my God, you have made me king in my father's place. But I am practically a child — I don't know the first thing about leading.

**8** And here I am, surrounded by your chosen people — a nation so vast it cannot be counted.

**9** So give me a heart that listens — one that can govern your people and tell right from wrong. For who could possibly govern this great people of yours?"

**10** The Lord was pleased that Solomon had asked for this.

**11** God said, "Because you asked for this — not for a long life, not for wealth, not for your enemies' death, but for discernment in administering justice —

**12** I am granting your request. I am giving you a mind so wise and perceptive that no one before you has ever had its equal, and no one after you ever will.

**13** And I am also giving you what you did not ask for — wealth and honor beyond any king of your time.

**14** And if you walk in my ways and obey my commands as your father David did, I will also give you a long life."

**15** Solomon woke up and realized it had been a dream. He went to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the LORD's covenant, and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. Then he held a banquet for all his court.

**16** Some time later, two prostitutes came before the king.

**17** One woman said, "My lord, this woman and I live in the same house. I had a baby while she was there with me.

**18** Three days later, she also had a baby. We were alone — no one else was in the house, just the two of us.

**19** During the night, her baby died because she rolled over on him.

**20** She got up in the middle of the night, took my son from beside me while I was sleeping, and put him at her breast. Then she put her dead son next to me.

**21** When I got up in the morning to nurse my baby, he was dead! But when I looked at him closely in the light, I saw it was not my son."

**22** "That's not true!" the other woman said. "The living baby is mine, and the dead one is yours!" "No!" the first insisted. "The dead one is yours, and the living one is mine!" They argued back and forth in front of the king.

**23** The king said, "So. One of you says, 'My son is alive, yours is dead.' The other says, 'No, your son is dead, mine is alive.'"

**24** Then the king said, "Bring me a sword." A sword was brought.

**25** The king said, "Cut the living child in two. Give half to one and half to the other."

**26** The real mother — her love for her son overwhelmed her — cried out, "Please, my lord! Give her the baby! Don't kill him!" But the other woman said, "Fair enough — neither of us gets him. Cut him in half."

**27** Then the king gave his ruling: "Give the baby to the first woman. Do not kill him. She is the mother."

**28** When all Israel heard about the king's verdict, they were in awe of him. They could see that he had God-given wisdom for doing justice.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **3:5 — "What do you want?"**: The most extraordinary offer in the Hebrew Bible. God gives Solomon a blank check. What a person asks for when they can have anything reveals who they truly are.

2. **3:7 — "practically a child"**: Solomon was likely in his late teens or early twenties. His self-assessment is honest and strategic — acknowledging limitation is itself a form of wisdom.

3. **3:9 — "a heart that listens"**: Not intelligence, not knowledge, not power — Solomon asks for the ability to hear. In Hebrew thought, wisdom begins with listening. This is the opposite of Saul, who could never hear what God was actually saying.

4. **3:14 — the fateful "if"**: Everything God gives Solomon is unconditional except one thing: length of life. This conditional clause is a seed that will bear bitter fruit. Solomon will get wisdom, wealth, and honor — but not old age on God's terms.

5. **3:26 — the real mother**: Solomon's test works because love and possessiveness produce opposite responses. The true mother would rather lose her child than see him die. The imposter would rather destroy the child than lose the argument.

— PNEUMA
